sessions.command.ask.desc: Ask before editing — read-only by default
sessions.command.plan.desc: Plan first, then execute on approval
sessions.command.compact.desc: Summarize older turns to free up token budget
sessions.command.style.desc: Pick a response style for this session
sessions.command.notice.nothingToCompact: Nothing more to compact — only recent messages remain, kept so you can continue
sessions.command.notice.compactFailed: Compaction failed — the conversation is unchanged
sessions.style.normal.name: Normal
sessions.style.normal.desc: The default — standard markdown formatting, with no special tone or structure applied.
sessions.style.military.name: Military
sessions.style.military.desc: Direct and factual — no preamble or filler, structured as problem → cause → fix. Best when you just want it fixed.
sessions.style.caveman.name: Caveman
sessions.style.caveman.hint: Code fast, keep the loop tight
sessions.style.caveman.desc: Ultra-terse caveman speech — short words, dropped articles, fragments — while the technical substance stays exact.
sessions.style.reality-check.name: Reality Check
sessions.style.reality-check.desc: An honest, balanced take on whether an idea is worth building — what works, the real risk, and a verdict: ship, rethink, or scrap.
sessions.style.step-by-step.name: Step by Step
sessions.style.step-by-step.desc: A numbered, sequential walkthrough — one concrete action per step, in the exact order they must happen. Best for procedures and how-tos where the order matters.
sessions.style.socratic.name: Socratic
sessions.style.socratic.desc: Never answers directly — asks questions that lead you to the answer yourself, confirming only once you get there. For learning, not copying.
sessions.style.bluf.name: BLUF
sessions.style.bluf.desc: Bottom Line Up Front — a one-sentence conclusion first, then the details. Best when comparing options and you want the verdict early.
sessions.style.checklist.name: Checklist
sessions.style.checklist.hint: Turn the answer into tasks to tick
sessions.style.checklist.desc: Turns the answer into a checklist of "- [ ]" tasks — one concrete step per line, no prose. Best when you want to act, not read.
sessions.style.code-first.name: Code First
sessions.style.code-first.hint: Just show the code, less chatter
sessions.style.code-first.desc: Leads with the code block and keeps prose minimal. The code carries the explanation; caveats go in brief bullets below.
sessions.style.yoda.name: Yoda
sessions.style.yoda.desc: Speaks like Yoda with inverted syntax. Technical accuracy stays intact and code is unchanged — just a little energy while debugging.
sessions.style.pirate.name: Pirate
sessions.style.pirate.hint: Team demo that needs a meme
sessions.style.pirate.desc: Talks like a pirate with nautical metaphors. Fun for a team demo; correctness is never sacrificed and code stays unchanged.
sessions.style.hacker-80s.name: 80s Hacker
sessions.style.hacker-80s.desc: Responds like a terminal in an 80s hacker movie — dramatic caps, > prompts, STATUS: labels. Theatrical but technically correct.
sessions.style.dad-joke.name: Dad Joke
sessions.style.dad-joke.hint: Teach a junior so it sticks
sessions.style.dad-joke.desc: Explains accurately, then ends every response with a terrible related dad joke. The explanation is real; the pun is a groaner.
sessions.style.noir.name: Noir
sessions.style.noir.desc: Answers like a hard-boiled noir detective: terse, moody, first-person. Atmospheric flavor; the technical substance stays exact.
sessions.style.speedrun.name: Speedrun
sessions.style.speedrun.desc: Narrates like a speedrunner — optimal route, skip the cutscenes, call out shortcuts and timesaves. Fast and hype, still exact.
sessions.style.corporate.name: Corporate
sessions.style.corporate.desc: Maximum corporate buzzword-speak with the technical content fully correct underneath. For a laugh at standup.
sessions.style.rubber-duck.name: Rubber Duck
sessions.style.rubber-duck.desc: Explains as if to a rubber duck — no jargon, every step broken down, zero assumed context. Best for a brand-new concept.
sessions.style.feynman.name: Feynman
sessions.style.feynman.desc: Uses the Feynman technique — explains to a curious 12-year-old, defining any jargon in plain English and building intuition before detail.
sessions.style.first-principles.name: First Principles
sessions.style.first-principles.desc: Breaks a problem down to fundamentals and rebuilds the reasoning from the ground up, never accepting conventional solutions unexamined.
sessions.style.devils-advocate.name: Devil's Advocate
sessions.style.devils-advocate.hint: Red-team my idea, push back hard
sessions.style.devils-advocate.desc: Argues against your idea as hard as it honestly can — failure modes, hidden costs, the case for not doing it — ending with the single strongest counter-argument. Stress-tests a decision; it won't propose alternatives or a verdict.
sessions.style.mentor.name: Mentor
sessions.style.mentor.hint: Explain the why + a next step
sessions.style.mentor.desc: Explains the "why" behind the "what", reaching for an analogy from your own domain only when it genuinely helps, then a small next step to try right now. Warm but honest about mistakes.
sessions.style.pair.name: Pair
sessions.style.pair.hint: Think out loud, dead ends and all
sessions.style.pair.desc: Narrates the reasoning out loud like a pairing partner — including the dead ends — instead of only the final answer.
sessions.pinned.title: Pinned context
sessions.pinned.hint: Files + notes re-fed into every turn of this session
sessions.pinned.notesPlaceholder: Notes always sent to the model…
sessions.pinned.savePresetTitle: Save these notes for reuse in any session
